summary_method: Medians of per-replay quantiles across alternating-order samples, not pooled frame percentiles. Count instrumentation runs only in separate documents.
conclusion: Predicate work decreases substantially for sequential/shuffled completion; reverse completion counts are unchanged. Native decode/draw elapsed results remain small and mixed; no universal browser latency improvement or Wi-Fi/physical-input claim. Initial6-sample and longer12-sample controls are both retained.

final.method: Actual Display/InputStream with native streamed PNG/WebP decode, real canvas draws, 40/128-image atomic frames and a 16ms minimum source interval. Separate count-only pages use controlled deferred-image callbacks and one instrumented readiness predicate.
final.limitations: Foreground headless Chrome decode-to-ACK-callback and browser-task opportunity; not physical paint/FPS/input, wire ACKs, transport, capture, Wi-Fi or background throttling. Pixel readback and pacing are outside per-frame timers. Count-only pages add predicate increments and provide structural work counts only, never speed evidence.
final.count_instrumentation: A separate document increments one counter at each tasks[index].blocked predicate read in Frame.isReady. Both sources receive the identical transformation; timing pages use unmodified sources. No production diagnostic/API is added.
